2310707.title: Department of Fisheries to Organize National Workshop on Promotion of Deep-Sea Fishing and Interaction with Access Pass and LoA Holders
2310707.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2310707.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Department of Fisheries to Organize National Workshop on Promotion of Deep-Sea Fishing and Interaction with Access Pass and LoA Holders
Major Focus on Technology, Financing, Skill development and Market Linkages promoting Harnessing of High-Value Marine Resources and Seafood Exports
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 9:54AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is organizing a National Workshop on Promotion of Deep-Sea Fishing and Interaction with Access Pass and LoA Holders on 17th September 2026 in Gandhinagar, Gujarat. The National workshop aims to promote deep-sea fishing by encouraging fishers to harness high-value fisheries resources, while also providing a platform to understand on-ground challenges and gather stakeholder suggestions for further strengthening the sector.

The National workshop will be graced by presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Gujarat, along with Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj. The event will also witness the participation of fishers including women fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Gujarat and all other coastal States/UTs, ICAR, CIFNET, NABARD, NCEL, NCDC, SEAI, MPEDA, EIC and other fisheries stakeholders.

Department of Fisheries, Government of India has given special thrust to strengthening fisheries farmer producer organizations (FFPO) and fisheries cooperatives while also focusing on digitization of the fisheries sector through various initiatives. 

The National workshop will feature focused technical sessions covering the entire deep-sea fishing value chain, from resource potential and vessel modernization to skill development, financing, processing, value addition and access to export markets. Discussions will explore opportunities for harnessing high-value fisheries resources in India’s EEZ and High Seas, adoption of modern fishing technologies and global best practices, capacity building for fishers and crew, access to institutional finance and cooperative-led investment models, and strengthening of post-harvest management, traceability, value addition, and export compliance systems. Each session will comprise expert presentations, fishers or industry perspectives, and stakeholder discussions, providing participants with practical insights and a comprehensive understanding of the opportunities, challenges, and support mechanisms available for advancing deep-sea fishing in India.

The deliberations are expected to serve as a significant platform for strengthening India’s deep-sea fishing ecosystem by bringing together policymakers, technical experts, financial institutions, industry stakeholders, cooperatives, and fishers for focused deliberations. The discussions and recommendations emerging from the workshop will help identify practical solutions to on-ground challenges, improve access to technology, skills, finance, and markets, and facilitate greater participation of fishers in deep-sea fishing.

 

Background

India is endowed with a vast and diverse marine resource base, supported by a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone of about 24 lakh sq. km. The marine fisheries potential within India’s EEZ is estimated at 58.6 lakh MT, supporting the livelihoods of approximately 50 lakh fishers and contributing significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation and export revenues. India is presently among the leading fisheries and aquaculture producing countries globally and exported seafood valued at around ₹73,890 crore during FY 2025-26.

Most fishing activities are concentrated within 40–50 nautical miles of the coast, while deeper waters and areas beyond national jurisdiction offer substantial opportunities for harvesting high-value species, particularly tuna and tuna-like resources. recognising the strategic importance of sustainable marine fisheries, the Government of India, has notified enabling framework including Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Rules, 2025 and High Seas Guidelines, 2025 for sustainable harnessing of fisheries resources by Indian-Flagged Fishing Vessels.

The Access Pass for fishing in India's EEZ, is a free digital pass issued via the ReALCRaft Portal. Its core objective is to empower the traditional fishers, cooperatives, and Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) for fishing in the EEZ (12 to 200 nautical miles), while ensuring sustainability of oceanic fishery resources. The Access Pass is issued under the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Rules, 2025 notified by the Government of India on 04 November 2025. The Access Pass is required for mechanized fishing vessels and large motorized boats over 24 meters length, while traditional non-motorized and small artisanal crafts are fully exempted to protect local livelihoods. This landmark initiative aims to empower traditional and small-scale fishermen, Fisheries Cooperative Societies, and Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to expand fishing operations, harness untapped resources through deep-sea fishing, and access new income streams through processing and exports, thereby enhancing livelihoods. As per the EEZ Rules, the Access Pass is required for undertaking fishing operations in the EEZ of India, beyond 12 nautical miles. So far, a total of 9,650 Access Passes have been issued based on applications received through coastal States and Union Territories.

2310697.title: CGST Delhi South Commissionerate busts firm for fraudulent availment of ITC of over Rs. 15.78 crore; arrests partner of firm
2310697.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
CGST Delhi South Commissionerate busts firm for fraudulent availment of ITC of over Rs. 15.78 crore; arrests partner of firm
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 9:56PM by PIB Delhi

As part of its ongoing enforcement drive against fraudulent Input Tax Credit (ITC) claims, the officers of Anti-Evasion Branch of the Central Goods & Services Tax (CGST), Delhi South Commissionerate, have arrested a partner of the firm engaged in trading of iron and steel goods in a case involving fraudulent availment, utilisation and passing on of inadmissible ITC aggregating to over Rs. 15.78 crore through bogus invoices of approximately Rs. 87.67 crore.

Investigation revealed that the firm had availed inadmissible ITC on the basis of invoices issued by multiple firms, several of which were found to be non-existent, non-functional, suspended or cancelled. Field verification also established that certain suppliers had no genuine business activity at their declared places of business.

Further inquiry established that ITC was availed without actual receipt of goods and was also passed on to various recipients through invoices issued without corresponding supply of goods.

Based on the evidence gathered during investigation and statements recorded under Section 70 of the CGST Act, 2017, the accused was arrested on 14.09.2026 under Section 69 of the CGST Act, 2017 and produced before the Patiala House Court, which remanded him to judicial custody for 14 days.

Further investigation in the case is under progress.

2310677.title: ‘Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari – Catch the Rain’ Anthem Released
2310677.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
‘Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari – Catch the Rain’ Anthem Released
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 8:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Jal Shakti today released the anthem for “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari – Catch the Rain”, giving a musical voice to the nationwide movement for water conservation and rainwater harvesting through people’s participation.

Sung by renowned singer-composer Shankar Mahadevan, the anthem carries at its heart the clarion call of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi: “Catch the Rain – Where It Falls, When It Falls.” Through an energetic and memorable message, it seeks to inspire citizens across the country to conserve rainwater and make Jal Sanchay a part of everyday life.

“पकड़ें हम, पकड़ें हम, बारिश का पानी,
लिखें हम, लिखें हम, एक नई कहानी।”

The anthem reflects a simple but powerful idea: water is life, and conserving it is a responsibility shared by all. Rainwater harvesting cannot be the responsibility of government alone. Lasting water security can be achieved only when every citizen, family, community, institution, local body and industry becomes an active participant in the effort.

Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari seeks to transform water conservation from a programme into a people-led movement. It encourages the creation and rejuvenation of rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge structures, while placing Jan Bhagidari at the centre of the country’s efforts to secure water for the future.

The anthem is intended to carry the Prime Minister’s message to every village, town, school, institution and household, particularly inspiring young people to become ambassadors of water conservation. It reminds citizens that every drop of rain conserved today contributes to stronger groundwater reserves, more resilient communities and a water-secure future.

The Ministry of Jal Shakti calls upon citizens across the country to join the movement and translate the message of the anthem into action. By catching the rain where it falls, when it falls, and by making water conservation a habit and a way of life, India can make Jal Sanchay a true Jan Andolan powered by Jan Bhagidari.

2310671.title: RSS’s Century of Service Reflects India’s Tradition of Seva: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan
2310671.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
RSS’s Century of Service Reflects India’s Tradition of Seva: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan
Vice President Releases Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan’s Book on RSS’s Century of Service
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 8:43PM by PIB Delhi

Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan today released the book “A Century of Service – The RSS in 100 Acts of Seva” authored by former Governor of Telangana and former Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry, Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan, at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi.

Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan today released the book “A Century of Service – The RSS in 100 Acts of Seva” authored by former Governor of Telangana and former Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry, Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan, at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi. pic.twitter.com/50z9TnIyID

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 15, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice President said the book documents the RSS’s century-long service, its social responsibility and its contribution to nation-building.

Observing that “today’s news is tomorrow’s history,” Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan stressed the importance of documenting good work, which could otherwise fade from public memory. He said the book captures how the spirit of seva has translated into sustained social service.

Describing “Seva is Dharma; it is a duty” as a foundational ideal, the Vice President said RSS service initiatives have reached the poor, marginalised and diverse sections of society, including workers, women and children. He recalled the role of RSS volunteers in providing food, medicines and essential support during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Referring to the theme of “Nation-building through character-building” in the book, the Vice President said patriotism, discipline, social responsibility and national unity are essential to nation-building.

He said the book would serve not only as a record of the RSS’s century-long service but also as a document reflecting India’s tradition of seva, culture and national consciousness for future generations.

The Vice President congratulated Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan and all those associated with the publication, expressing hope that more such efforts to document history would follow.

Union Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan; Puducherry Home Minister Shri A. Namassivayam; Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan; were present.

2310670.title: Department of Pharmaceuticals Observes Swachhata Pakhwada with Cleanliness Drives Across Offices, NIPERs and PSUs
2310670.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals
2310670.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Department of Pharmaceuticals Observes Swachhata Pakhwada with Cleanliness Drives Across Offices, NIPERs and PSUs
Reinforces Commitment to Cleanliness and Hygiene During Swachhata Pakhwada
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 8:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, observed Swachhata Pakhwada from September 1 to 15, 2026, with active participation of officers and employees across the Department, NIPERs and PSUs. Pakhwada was observed in line with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for “Swachh Bharat, Swasth Bharat”, emphasising cleanliness, hygiene and collective responsibility towards maintaining clean and healthy surroundings.

The Swachhata Pakhwada commenced on September 1, 2026, with Secretary, Department of Pharmaceuticals, Shri Manoj Joshi, administering the Swachhata pledge to officers of the Department. During the Pakhwada, a series of cleanliness and awareness activities were undertaken by the Department. Officers and staff participated in cleanliness drives at their respective workstations and office premises.

As part of the initiative, senior officers and staff of the Department, led by Joint Secretary Shri Aman Sharma, undertook Shramdaan at the Janpath Bhawan Market, New Delhi.

The Department also undertook a comprehensive review of old and redundant items, including furniture, fixtures and electronic items, for their repair, disposal and systematic management. A pest-control drive was also conducted at offices.

The Swachhata Pakhwada witnessed active participation at all the seven National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPERs). Cleanliness drives were organised across campuses, with faculty members, students and staff coming together to clean and maintain their respective institutional premises. In a few campuses, plantation activities were also undertaken.

Cleanliness activities were also undertaken at PSUs under the department in various places. Employees participated in Swachhata drives.

The Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India observed Swachta Pakhwada in its office premises and the cleanliness campaign was further extended to Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country. These initiatives helped reinforce the message that clean surroundings are an essential component of public health and well-being.

The Swachhata Pakhwada brought together officers, employees, students, faculty members and others in a collective effort towards cleanliness. The Department reaffirmed the spirit of “Swachh Bharat, Swasth Bharat” and underscored the importance of sustained participation and responsible practices to create cleaner workplaces and communities.

2310643.title: INDIAN PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATION PARTICIPATES IN 69TH COMMONWEALTH PARLIAMENTARY CONFERENCE IN CAPE TOWN FROM 12 TO 19 SEPTEMBER 2026
2310643.body_html:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
INDIAN PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATION PARTICIPATES IN 69TH COMMONWEALTH PARLIAMENTARY CONFERENCE IN CAPE TOWN FROM 12 TO 19 SEPTEMBER 2026
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi

An Indian Parliamentary Delegation led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha is participating in the 69th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference (CPC) being held in Cape Town, South Africa, from 12 to 19 September 2026.

The Indian Parliamentary Delegation comprises Shri C. Sadanandan Master, MP, Rajya Sabha; Dr. D. Purandeswari, MP, Lok Sabha; Shri Vishnu Datt Sharma, MP, Lok Sabha; Shri Sudheer Gupta, MP, Lok Sabha; Shri Krishna Prasad Tenneti, MP, Lok Sabha; Smt. Rachna Banerjee, MP, Lok Sabha; and Shri P. C. Mody, Secretary General, Rajya Sabha.

The Conference is also being attended by 32 Presiding Officers and 18 Secretaries from State/UT Legislatures of India, who are members of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA).

Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, arrived in Cape Town today and held bilateral meeting with Hon. Angela Thokozile Didiza, Speaker of the National Assembly, Hon. Poobalan Govender, Deputy Chairperson of the National Council of Provinces of South Africa and Hon. Annelie Lotriet, Deputy Speaker of National Assembly. The meetings provided an opportunity to exchange views on matters of mutual parliamentary interest and to further strengthen the close and longstanding parliamentary relations between India and South Africa.

Further, Dr. D. Purandeswari, MP, Lok Sabha, attended the meeting of the CPA Executive Committee and effectively put forth India’s views and perspectives on various matters concerning the CPA.

During the Conference, six main workshops will inter-alia be held on a range of contemporary issues of relevance to Commonwealth legislatures. Shri Harivansh will address the General Assembly of the 69th CPC on the theme, “New Leadership Opportunities for the Commonwealth: Parliamentary Action to Strengthen Democracy and International Law.”

Members of the Indian Parliamentary Delegation, along with Presiding Officers and other representatives from State/UT Legislatures, will participate in the various workshops, plenary sessions and deliberations of the General Assembly during the Conference.

India’s participation in the 69th CPC reflects its continued commitment to strengthening parliamentary democracy, legislative cooperation and inter-parliamentary engagement within the Commonwealth, while further deepening the strong parliamentary ties between India and South Africa.

The Indian delegation will continue its participation in the Conference in the coming days, including in the General Assembly and various workshops addressing issues of contemporary global and parliamentary relevance.

2310618.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported assault and public humiliation of a woman by her husband and other relatives in Banswara, Rajasthan
2310618.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported assault and public humiliation of a woman by her husband and other relatives in Banswara, Rajasthan
Issues notices to the Chief Secretary, Government of Rajasthan and the Superintendent of Police, Banswara, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 7:34PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India, has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report brought to its notice that a woman was beaten with sticks and paraded semi-nude after forcibly cutting her hair by her husband and other relatives in Banswara, Rajasthan on 1st September 2026. Reportedly, they were accusing her of leaving home with another man.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the media report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of the victim’s rights to life and dignity. Accordingly, notices have been issued to the Chief Secretary, Government of Rajasthan and the Superintendent of Police, Banswara, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the victim.

According to the media report, carried on 04th September 2026, the matter came to light after a video of the incident surfaced on social media. Reportedly, the woman was subjected to cruelty and inhuman treatment in full public view.

2310611.title: 95% physical files and 87.5% e-files reviewed under Special Campaign 5.0 by Department of Higher Education
2310611.body_html:
Ministry of Education
95% physical files and 87.5% e-files reviewed under Special Campaign 5.0 by Department of Higher Education
Department gears up to organize Special Campaign 6.0 from October 2 to 31, 2026
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Higher Education (DoHE), Union Ministry of Education, reviewed 95.2% (2,04,859) of physical files and 87.46% (62,564) of e-files under Special Campaign 5.0. Around 1,159 sites were covered across the country under the Campaign, making significant progress in reducing pendency, freeing 14,44,839 sq. ft. of office space and improving record management. DoHE also generated ₹6.89 crore worth of revenue through scrap disposal. Over 3,312 files were digitized and 90,629 physical/electronic files were weeded out/closed.

DoHE is now set to actively participate in Special Campaign 6.0, from October 2 to 31, 2026 aimed at promoting Swachhata across all offices, including autonomous organizations, by reducing pendency matters in offices and centrally funded HEIs, enhancing the cleanliness of government offices and improving the overall workplace environment.

Special Campaign 6.0 will proceed in two phases: Preparatory Phase from September 15 to 30, 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from October 2 to 31, 2026. Heads/faculties of centrally funded Institutions, UGC, AICTE and Bureaus of DoHE are setting specific targets, identifying pending references, and outlining key areas for cleanliness and space management during the Preparatory Phase. Special attention will be given to record management, disposal of outdated materials and the beautification of offices. In furtherance of the previous year’s focus on the scientific management of e-waste, the Campaign this year will emphasize on "effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste”.

The Implementation Phase will focus on clearing pending matters, including public grievances, parliamentary assurances and inter-ministerial communications and VVIP references. Participating offices will be required to report their progress on a daily basis. The Campaign also aims to promote sustainability and foster greater public engagement through social media, using the hashtag #SpecialCampaign6.

As part of a Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters orgainsed from November, 2025 to August, 2026, a significant volume of public interface matters, including 24,126 public grievances and 4,177 public grievance appeals, were disposed of.

2310610.title: Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture inaugurates new Training Programs at Institute of Archaeology
2310610.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture inaugurates new Training Programs at Institute of Archaeology
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture inaugurated the Induction Training Programme for newly recruited Senior Conservation Assistants and Conservation Assistants at the Institute of Archaeology, Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Campus, Greater Noida today. This is a one-month intensive training program for 53 newly recruited Senior Conservation Assistants (Sr. CA) and Conservation Assistants (CA) from various ASI Circles across the country. The revamped curriculum fuses core archaeological practices with administrative decision-making, training officers in Government Financial Rules (GFR), administrative law, establishment procedures, manpower-management, and departmental inquiries.

While addressing the trainees, the Secretary articulated a strategic shift to transform the Institute into an International Centre of Excellence. He stressed the need for harnessing India's protected monuments as economic catalysts. Highlighting the "Monument Economy," the Secretary underscored that cultural heritage directly generates employment and contributes to national GDP by stimulating tourism, local transport, hospitality, artisan markets, light-and-sound shows, and curated heritage walks etc., directly or through public-private partnerships (PPPs).

The Secretary exhorted the officers to embrace decisive leadership. He stressed that institutional resources are no barrier for initiatives taken up in right earnest. He further outlined the ethos of prioritizing national interest (Desh Hit) first, institutional duty (Sanstha Hit) second, and society and family (Samaj aur Parivar) third.

Director General, ASI, Shri Yadubir Singh Rawat reiterated the governing conservation philosophy of "Minimum intervention and Maximum retention". He also announced that this module will soon be followed by refresher courses for in-service ASI personnel and state archaeology department officials.

The initiative marks a significant milestone in a rejuvenation drive to fully utilize the Institute of Archaeology’s state-of-the-art, 25-acre campus. Transitioning beyond its traditional 15-student Post Graduate Diploma in Archaeology (PGDA) cohort, the Institute is now being repositioned as a premier Archaeological training Institution, which at its maturity would be, comparable to the best training institutions in the world. The campus will also be developed as a hub for cultural activities in the area and for educating young students about the life and work of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya.

2310608.title: Railway Minister Inaugurates Shivlakha GCT, Dedicates Three Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals to the Nation and Lays Foundation Stone for Linch GCT
2310608.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Railway Minister Inaugurates Shivlakha GCT, Dedicates Three Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals to the Nation and Lays Foundation Stone for Linch GCT
New GCTs to Support Faster Cargo Movement, Reduce Logistics Costs and Connect Regional Businesses with National Markets
Union Minister also Flags Off  Salt-Loaded Freight Train from Shivlakha GCT to Mithapur
Lightweight Stainless Steel Salt Containers to Make Salt Loading, Unloading and Transportation Easier
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw today inaugurated, dedicated to the nation and laid the foundation stone for five Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals (GCTs) in Gujarat, strengthening the State’s freight handling capacity and improving connectivity between regional economic centres, ports and markets across the country.

Shri Vaishnaw also flagged off the  salt-loaded freight train from Shivlakha GCT to  Mithapur, marking an important step towards greater use of rail for movement of salt from Gujarat to its destination.

Among the five GCTs, the GCT at Shivlakha in Kachchh was inaugurated . The GCT at Bhimasar in Kachchh, the GCT at Devaliya in Morbi, and the GCT at Chandisar in Banaskantha were dedicated to the nation. The foundation stone was laid for the GCT at Linch in Mahesana.

 

माननीय रेल मंत्री श्री @AshwiniVaishnaw जी ने आज गुजरात में स्थित पांच गति शक्ति कार्गो टर्मिनल का शिलान्यास, उद्धाटन एवं राष्ट्र को समर्पण किया।#RailInfra4Gujarat#FreightFriendlyRailways pic.twitter.com/KmdpEpqi67

— Ministry of Railways (@RailMinIndia) September 15, 2026

 

These terminals will help expand rail capacity for freight movement, reduce congestion and bottlenecks at port locations and strengthen freight connectivity between the ports of Gujarat and the northern hinterland. By connecting local economic centres with wider national markets and ports, the GCTs will support growing industrial, trade and business activity in the region.

Highlighting the importance of salt transportation, Shri Vaishnaw mentioned that salt is an essential commodity consumed by every household, including poor and middle-class families. He said Gujarat, particularly Kachchh, is a major salt-producing region and transporting salt to different parts of the country has traditionally posed several challenges.

Shri Vaishnaw highlighted that when salt was transported in conventional railway wagons, a significant portion of the wagon's carrying capacity was taken up by the wagon itself. Further, salt tends to absorb moisture, resulting in the cargo becoming wet during transportation. This created difficulties during loading and unloading. He further explained that the new light weight stainless steel salt container has been designed specifically to address these challenges. The container allows loading from the top and unloading from the side. He said the new containers will make it easier to transport salt to different parts of the country, while making the loading and unloading process smoother and more efficient.

Shri Vaishnaw said that 150 Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals have now been commissioned across the country, providing benefits to industries and improving freight connectivity.

Speaking about railway infrastructure in Kachchh, Shri Vaishnaw said that railway projects worth around ₹5,600 crore are currently underway in the Kachchh region. He highlighted the capacity augmentation and doubling works on important sections connecting Samakhiali, Bhachau, Gandhidham, Adipur and Bhuj. He said the Bhuj-Naliya gauge conversion project has strengthened rail connectivity in the region. He added that the Naliya-Jakhau Port new broad-gauge line has also been sanctioned, which will further improve connectivity in the region.

Speaking about railway infrastructure in the Kandla-Gandhidham industrial region, Shri Vaishnaw said rail connectivity is being strengthened through capacity augmentation works. He said the Samakhiali-Bhachau section has already been made four-line. The Gandhidham-Adipur section has already been made four-line, while the Adipur-Bhuj single-line section is being doubled.

The Railway Minister added that the Bhuj-Naliya section has recently been converted from metre gauge to broad gauge. Shri Vaishnaw said the railway network from Naliya towards Jakhau Port, Vayor, Luna, Hajipur and Desalpar is also being developed further.

Shri Vaishnaw said the expanded railway network will provide significant benefits to the Kachchh region, particularly for the requirements of the defence sector and industry. It will also benefit residents living in this challenging terrain. Together, these initiatives strengthen both freight and passenger infrastructure in Gujarat, improve access to rail services and cargo facilities, and create greater opportunities for industries, businesses and local communities to benefit from efficient rail connectivity.

Referring to Dedicated Freight Corridors, Shri Vaishnaw mentioned the recently commissioned infrastructure would provide significant benefits for freight transportation by enabling faster and more efficient movement of goods. He added that work on expanding east-west freight connectivity is also being pursued.

On the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail project, Shri Vaishnaw said construction on the Vapi-Surat section is targeted by December 2026. He added that testing and other associated works would follow. Shri Vaishnaw said the first coach of India's indigenous high-speed train has been prepared and is undergoing various tests. He added that the train is being developed as part of the country's efforts towards Atmanirbhar Bharat and greater indigenisation of high-speed rail technology.

The event was attended by Shri Trikambhai Chhanga, Hon’ble Minister of State, Government of Gujarat; Shri Vinodbhai Chavda, Hon’ble Member of Parliament; Shri Haribhai Patel, Hon’ble Member of Parliament; Shri Rajubhai Shukla, Hon’ble Member of Parliament; Shri Chandubhai Shihora, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, along with other officials and dignitaries.

2310605.title: India’s Largest-Ever Skilled Youth Contingent Flagged Off for WorldSkills Shanghai 2026
2310605.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2310605.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
India’s Largest-Ever Skilled Youth Contingent Flagged Off for WorldSkills Shanghai 2026
70-member Team India to compete across 63 skills at the world’s foremost skills competition
India to make its debut in 11 new-age and emerging skill categories
Viksit Bharat–Kushal Bharat will be realised through skilled, confident and innovative young Indians: Shri Jayant Chaudhary
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, today hosted the send-off ceremony for the Indian contingent participating in WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi.

India’s largest-ever contingent of 70 skilled young competitors will represent the country across 63 skill categories at the 48th WorldSkills Competition, scheduled to be held in Shanghai, China, from 22 to 27 September 2026. The competitors will showcase India’s growing capabilities in technical excellence, creativity, precision, innovation and craftsmanship on the world stage.

The ceremony was graced by Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India; Shri Kapil Dev Aggarwal, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh; Shri Ashish Sood, Minister for Home, Education, Power, Urban Development, Higher Education, and Training & Technical Education, Government of NCT of Delhi; and Shri Naveen Jindal, Member of Parliament and Chairman, Jindal Steel.

Also present were Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE; Shri Dilip Kumar, Director General, Directorate General of Training; Shri Niranjan Kumar Sudhansu, Additional Secretary, MSDE; Ms. Manisha Sensarma, Senior Economic Adviser, MSDE; Shri Arunkumar Pillai, Chief Executive Officer, National Skill Development Corporation, along with senior government officials, representatives of industry and training institutions, experts, mentors, competitors and their families.

Addressing Team India, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education said, “Team India represents a confident, creative and digitally agile generation, ready to compete with the world’s best. Our participation in new-age skills reflects the growing depth of India’s skilling ecosystem. Guided by the Prime Minister’s vision, the Government is taking skilling to scale through skill competitions, Kaushal Mahotsavs and stronger partnerships with States and industry. At some point in time, we must aspire to host such global skill competitions as well. To our competitors, I say- trust your training, stay focused and compete without fear. Shanghai is not only a competition; it is an opportunity to discover how far your skill can take you. Embrace the spirit of ‘Never Give Up’, give your very best and inspire a generation to choose skill with confidence and pride.” In a gesture celebrating unity and team spirit, Shri Jayant Chaudhary wore the newly unveiled India competitor attire that Team India will don at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026.

Shri Kapil Dev Aggarwal, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the State’s continued support for the Skill India Mission through quality training, entrepreneurship promotion and stronger industry linkages. He expressed pride in the participation of Uttar Pradesh’s talented youth in Team India at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 and reaffirmed the State Government’s commitment to working closely with the Central Government to expand skilling opportunities across every district and enable young people to excel nationally and globally.

Highlighting the importance of bridging the gap between education, skills and employment, Shri Ashish Sood, Minister for Home, Education, Power, Urban Development, Higher Education, and Training & Technical Education, Government of NCT of Delhi, noted that Team India’s participation at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 demonstrates how structured training and access to the right opportunities can enable young people to achieve global excellence. He emphasised the need to provide students with practical exposure and clear pathways to employment and entrepreneurship, while reaffirming the Delhi Government’s commitment to working closely with the Central Government to advance the shared skilling agenda and prepare youth for a rapidly evolving economy.

Commenting on the association, Shri Naveen Jindal, Chairman, Jindal Steel, said, “India’s young skill champions embody confidence, discipline and the determination to excel. We are proud to support Team India as they carry the nation’s aspirations to WorldSkills Shanghai 2026. I wish every competitor the very best as they showcase Indian talent and excellence before the world.” Jindal Steel is the Official Merchandise Sponsor for Team India’s WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 campaign, supporting the ceremonial and competition attire of the Indian competitors.

For the first time, India will compete in 11 new skill categories: Dental Prosthetics, Digital Interactive Media Design, Intelligent Security Technology, Landscape Gardening, Optoelectronic Technology, Retail Sales, Unmanned Aerial Systems, Industrial Mechanics, Software Testing, Heavy Vehicle Technology and Aircraft Maintenance. India’s participation reflects the growing depth and maturity of its skilling ecosystem, which is expanding beyond conventional trades into complex technologies, specialised services and next-generation industrial capabilities.

The preparation of Team India has been supported by a wide network of State Governments, Sector Skill Councils, training institutions, industry partners, experts and mentors. Through specialised facilities, equipment, technical expertise, simulations and international exposure, these partners have helped competitors train according to exacting global standards.

The ceremony also witnessed the announcement of first cohort of 16 members to the WorldSkills India Champions Club, bringing together distinguished former competitors and medallists as ambassadors of India’s skills movement. The Club will enable these champions to mentor aspiring competitors, share their experiences and inspire more young people to pursue skills with confidence, excellence and pride.

WorldSkills is the world’s leading platform for recognising and promoting excellence in vocational skills. The Shanghai edition will bring together more than 1,400 young competitors from over 60 countries and regions, competing across 64 skill competitions.

India’s performance at international skill competitions has shown consistent progress. The country moved from the 29th position in 2015 to the 13th position at WorldSkills Lyon 2024, where it secured four Bronze Medals and 12 Medallions for Excellence. India also secured the eighth position in Asia at WorldSkills Asia 2025.

As the 70-member contingent departs for Shanghai, it carries the aspirations of the nation, the expertise of its trainers and mentors, the support of industry and institutions, and the encouragement of families across India. Team India is ready to demonstrate to the world that the future belongs to those who can create, build, innovate and perform with skill.

***

2310588.title: NDSA Reviews Dam Safety Preparedness and Implementation of Dam Safety Act in Jharkhand
2310588.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
NDSA Reviews Dam Safety Preparedness and Implementation of Dam Safety Act in Jharkhand
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

A team of the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA), led by Shri Saurabh Agrawal, Member (Administration & Finance), NDSA, comprising Shri Manoj Kumar, Senior Joint Commissioner, Department of Water Resources, RD&GR, Ministry of Jal Shakti and Shri Amitabh Meena, Director (Technical), NDSA, held a meeting with the Secretary, Water Resources Department, Government of Jharkhand, on September 8, 2026, to review the implementation of the Dam Safety Act, 2021 and the status of dam safety activities in the State.

The meeting was attended by the Head of the State Dam Safety Organisation (SDSO) and representatives of dam owners from the Water Resources Department, Energy Department and Drinking Water & Sanitation Department (DW&SD) of Jharkhand.

The status of Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation (CDSE) of specified dams in Jharkhand was reviewed. NDSA emphasised the need for expeditious constitution of the Independent Panel of Experts (IPoE), timely completion of dam visits and submission of CDSE reports to the Authority. The State was also requested to prepare and furnish a dam-wise action plan for completion of CDSE within the prescribed timeline.

The meeting also reviewed the status of Emergency Action Plans (EAPs) and Operation & Maintenance (O&M) Manuals. Instructions were issued for their timely preparation and subsequent uploading on the DHARMA Portal. The inspection status of Category-II dams was also reviewed and a time bound action plan for rehabilitation of such dams was sought.

NDSA emphasised strengthening of the State's institutional framework for dam safety, including reconstitution of the SDSO as a dedicated organisation rather than a committee-based arrangement. The need for operationalisation of a separate budget head for dam safety and appropriate allocation and utilisation of funds was also emphasised. Capacity-building programmes for dam owners and SDSO personnel were highlighted as an important requirement for strengthening dam safety preparedness in the State.

The importance of timely laying of the SDSO Report before the State Legislature, as required under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, was also emphasised. Representatives of the Energy Department and DW&SD were advised to ensure compliance with the provisions of the Dam Safety Act, 2021 applicable to dam owners under their respective jurisdictions.

The dam owner of Nalkari Dam (Patratu), under the Energy Department, was specifically directed to constitute a Dam Safety Unit (DSU) and undertake pre-monsoon and post-monsoon inspections in accordance with the applicable dam safety regulations.

The Secretary, Water Resources Department, assured the Authority that necessary action would be taken for time bound implementation of the Dam Safety Act, 2021. He directed Head SDSO Jharkhand to prepare a dam wise action plan covering CDSE, EAPs and rehabilitation of Category-II dams and furnish the same to NDSA.

As part of the field level review, the NDSA team visited Nalkari Dam on September 8, 2026 and Latratu Dam, a Category-II dam under the Water Resources Department, on September 9, 2026. The team reviewed the safety aspects and preparedness at the dams. Necessary instructions were issued to the concerned dam in-charges for rectification of deficiencies observed during the visits.

The review reflects NDSA's continued efforts towards strengthening dam safety governance, ensuring compliance with the Dam Safety Act, 2021 and promoting timely preventive and rehabilitative measures for ensuring the safety of dams and downstream communities in the country.

2310586.title: UPI Continues to Remain Free for Peer to Peer Transactions and 96% of Merchant Transactions
2310586.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
UPI Continues to Remain Free for Peer to Peer Transactions and 96% of Merchant Transactions
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi

The new UPI framework introduced has no impact on any person to person transactions. UPI will continue to remain completely free for all person-to-person transactions, irrespective of the amount transferred.

Payments to merchants up to ₹2,000, along with transactions covered under the zero-MDR framework for small merchants, will also remain free. Consequently, approximately 96% of all P2M transactions will remain unaffected. MDR will apply only to specified merchant transactions above ₹2,000.

It is clarified that MDR is neither a tax nor a charge collected by the Government or NPCI. It is distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and payment application providers, to support the operation and continued expansion of the UPI ecosystem.

Introduced under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, following detailed deliberations by the UPI Steering Committee, the framework seeks to ensure the long-term sustainability of UPI while protecting individuals and small merchants from additional charges.

  1. What Will Remain Free

All Person-to-Person Transactions: All person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will remain completely free, irrespective of the amount transferred. No transaction fee, platform fee or other charge may be imposed on individuals for sending or receiving money through UPI. Therefore, UPI transactions accounting for 70% of the total transaction value will remain completely outside the MDR framework.

Merchant Payments Up to ₹2,000: All person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions up to ₹2,000 will remain free of MDR. Customers will not be required to pay any charge when making such payments through UPI.

Payments Received by Small Merchants: Small merchants including street vendors receiving up to ₹1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes under the Person-to-Person-Merchant (P2PM) category will continue to enjoy zero MDR on all transactions. This provision will protect street vendors, neighbourhood shops and other small businesses from additional payment costs.

  1. What Will Attract MDR

Merchant Transactions Above ₹2,000: A nominal MDR of 0.4% will apply only to P2M transactions above ₹2,000. The MDR will be shared among payment ecosystem participants, including banks, payment service providers and UPI application providers. For transactions of ₹75,000 and above, the MDR will be capped at ₹300 per transaction.

Transactions in Essential Sectors: Transactions above ₹2,000 in essential and thin-margin sectors, including railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will attract a flat MDR of ₹5 per transaction. The flat charge will provide cost certainty for critical public services and businesses operating on narrow margins.

Capital Market Transactions: Payments relating to mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers and dealers will attract an MDR of 0.02%, capped at ₹300 per transaction. The lower rate is intended to support continued retail participation in formal financial markets.

  1. Customers Will Not Pay MDR

MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments.

Banks have been advised to ensure that merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges.

Individuals will continue to have unlimited free usage, with no monthly quotas, volume restrictions or tiered caps on free UPI transactions.

Daily transaction limits prescribed by banks and NPCI, generally ranging from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh depending on the transaction category, are security and risk-management safeguards. They are not charging thresholds.

  1. Most Merchant Transactions Will Remain Unaffected

Data analysis indicates that MDR will apply to only about 4% of merchant transactions.

This means that approximately 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected, as they are either below the ₹2,000 threshold or covered by the zero-MDR framework for small merchants.

The framework therefore protects individuals, micro-enterprises and small businesses while introducing a limited charge on larger merchant transactions.

  1. Support for Small Merchants

A dedicated fund will be established to promote UPI adoption among small merchants. An amount equivalent to 5% of total MDR collections will be contributed to this fund.

The fund will support wider UPI acceptance, sustained usage and the inclusion of small businesses in India’s digital payments ecosystem.

  1. Ensuring the Continued Growth of UPI

The framework has been introduced under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, following detailed deliberations by the UPI Steering Committee on the applicable rates, operational arrangements and consumer safeguards.

The framework seeks to strengthen the long-term sustainability of UPI while keeping payments free for individuals and protecting small merchants.

Revenue generated from larger merchant transactions will support banks, payment service providers and UPI application providers in expanding and improving payment infrastructure, including in rural and semi-urban areas.

The framework is also consistent with the recommendation of the Standing Committee on Finance in its 32nd Report, which emphasised the importance of a viable revenue.

2310585.title: Ministry of Law and Justice organises Officer-Level Awareness Workshop on Tele-Law Services at Nuh, Haryana under DISHA 2.0 Scheme
2310585.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Ministry of Law and Justice organises Officer-Level Awareness Workshop on Tele-Law Services at Nuh, Haryana under DISHA 2.0 Scheme
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, organized an Officer-Level Awareness Workshop under the Tele-Law Initiative of the DISHA 2.0 (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice) Scheme at the Mini Secretariat, Nuh, Haryana on 15 September 2026. The workshop was chaired by Shri Suresh Kumar, Joint Secretary, Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice and SDM of Nuh Shri Kunwar Aditya Vikram, CSC Vice President along with other representatives of the Common Services Centres (CSCs), Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs), Panel Lawyers, Nyaya Sahayaks and other key stakeholders working towards strengthening access to Justice at the grassroots level. A number of 150 participants attended the Awareness Workshop.

The Awareness workshop was organised with the objective of enhancing awareness about the Tele-Law programme, promoting the use of technology-enabled legal services, and strengthening coordination among stakeholders involved in the delivery of legal assistance to citizens, particularly those residing in rural and underserved areas.

The programme commenced with an inaugural session comprising an opening remarks by the Chair, Joint Secretary, Department of Justice. This was followed by a presentation on the DISHA 2.0 Scheme, highlighting its vision of advancing access to Justice through the integrated implementation of Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, Legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Programme (LLLAP), and VIDHI-Sanjeevani.

During the technical session, participants were briefed on the functioning and impact of the Tele-Law Services, the role of Common Services Centres (CSCs) as grassroots access points for legal assistance, and the contribution of Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) in facilitating legal consultations for citizens. The session also emphasized the importance of leveraging digital platforms to bridge the gap between legal service providers and beneficiaries.

A live demonstration of the Tele-Law Portal and the Nyaya Setu AI-enabled chatbot was conducted to familiarize participants with the digital tools available under the scheme and to showcase how citizens can access legal information and advice through technology-driven platforms.

The Awareness workshop concluded with an interactive stakeholder discussion focusing on implementation challenges, best practices, and opportunities for expanding the reach of legal services. Participants also shared suggestions and raised queries regarding the effective delivery of Tele-Law services in their respective jurisdictions.

The workshop concluded with a vote of thanks by Shri. Gaurav Kumar Tripathi, Under Secretary, Department of Justice reaffirming the collective commitment of all stakeholders towards strengthening access to justice and promoting legal empowerment across the country.

2310584.title: NSTFDC signed Memorandum of Understanding with HPCL for establishment of Computer Lab-cum-Smart Classroom in 29 Eklavya Model Residential Schools in Rajasthan
2310584.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
NSTFDC signed Memorandum of Understanding with HPCL for establishment of Computer Lab-cum-Smart Classroom in 29 Eklavya Model Residential Schools in Rajasthan
Integrated technology-enabled learning facilities to benefit more than 10,000 Scheduled Tribe students annually
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 6:27PM by PIB Delhi

The National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for establishment of integrated Computer Lab-cum-Smart Classroom facilities in 29 functional Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) across 11 districts of Rajasthan.

The MoU was signed in the presence of Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, MoTA; Shri T. Roumuan Paite, Joint Secretary, MoTA and CMD, NSTFDC; Shri Ganesh Nagarajan, Deputy Secretary, MoTA, and other senior officials of MoTA. The HPCL delegation included Shri K.S. Shetty, Director (HR); Shri Pawan Kumar Sehgal, CGM, DCO; Shri Anupam Tiwari, CGM, CSR & PRCC; Shri Bhargav Chauhan, Manager, CSR; and Ms. Sakshi Dwivedi, Officer, CSR, while the NSTFDC delegation comprised Ms. Bismita Das, AGM, Projects & CSR; Shri Himanshu Vishwakarma, Chief Manager, and Shri Vikash Ranjan, Manager, Projects & CSR.

The project, with a total budget of ₹16.01 crore approved by the HPCL Board, is planned to be completed within six months from the date of signing of the MoU.

Under the project, each school will have four smart classrooms equipped with 86-inch interactive flat panels, pre-loaded licensed software, curated open educational resources and audio-visual equipment, including speakers and webcams. Each school will also have a fully networked computer laboratory with desktops and UPS backup, structured LAN, multi-function printer, furniture, air-conditioning, electrical refurbishment and safety systems.

In addition, 10 tablets pre-loaded with coaching material for competitive examinations will be provided in each school. Internet connectivity, including wiring, installation and a one-year subscription, will also be provided.

The 29 EMRSs covered under the project are located in Alwar, Banswara, Baran, Dungarpur, Jaipur, Karauli, Pratapgarh, Sawai Madhopur, Sirohi, Tonk and Udaipur. The schools will benefit more than 10,000 Scheduled Tribe students every year, with equal representation of girls. At full sanctioned capacity, the schools can accommodate up to 13,920 students, from Classes VI to XII, most of whom are first-generation digital learners.

The initiative aligns with the National Education Policy 2020, which mandates the integration of technology in teaching-learning, digital literacy for all, and computational thinking and coding from the middle stage, with targeted support to socio-economically disadvantaged groups, including tribal children. The project also conforms to the common theme of “Innovative Livelihood Enhancement” prescribed by the Department of Public Enterprises for CSR activities of CPSEs during 2026–27 and 2027–28.

Addressing the gathering, the Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, highlighted the transformative role of education in enabling multi-generational progress. The Secretary noted that EMR are creating pathways for tribal students towards higher education and diverse careers, and expressed confidence that the HPCL-supported initiative will strengthen access to technology and opportunities for higher learning.

The project will leverage the institutional ecosystem of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, with NSTFDC responsible for implementation and procurement, NESTS for academic validation and prevention of duplication, and the State EMRS Society and school Principals for site readiness and day-to-day use.

The Secretary expressed gratitude to HPCL and the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas for supporting the initiative and described the partnership as an example of whole-of-government working together for the tribal cause.

2310567.title: Defence Accounts Department Achieves 100% Normalization of Air Force and Navy Pension Cases on SPARSH
2310567.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Defence Accounts Department Achieves 100% Normalization of Air Force and Navy Pension Cases on SPARSH
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

Defence Accounts Department (DAD) has achieved a remarkable milestone in the normalization of discrepant pension cases on SPARSH (System for Pension Administration – Raksha) through a focused and concentrated approach. As part of a special drive, undertaken in mission mode with close monitoring, focused examination of cases and coordinated action by the concerned offices, the Department has successfully normalized all 1,45,182 discrepant cases pertaining to the Indian Air Force and Indian Navy.

The cases normalized include:

  • Indian Air Force: 1,12,638 cases – 100%
  • Indian Navy: 32,544 cases – 100%

The Department has simultaneously made substantial progress in normalization of discrepant cases pertaining to the Indian Army; Out of a total of 3,94,779 discrepant cases, 3,90,336 cases, constituting 98.8%, have already been normalized on SPARSH.

The achievement is a reflection of the dedication, coordinated efforts and result-oriented approach of DAD, particularly the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) and Principal Controller of Defence Accounts (Pension) [PCDA (Pension)], towards strengthening the SPARSH ecosystem.

2310540.title: CAQM reviews Enforcement and Compliance Status across NCR; 150 Inspections conducted during 15-day reporting period
2310540.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2310540.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM reviews Enforcement and Compliance Status across NCR; 150 Inspections conducted during 15-day reporting period
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

The 139th meeting of the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), held on 14.09.2026, reviewed enforcement actions, inspections and compliance status across the National Capital Region (NCR) for the reporting period from 24.08.2026 to 07.09.2026. During the 15-day reporting period, a total of 150 inspections were reported, including 7 inspections at Construction and Demolition (C&D) sites, 98 inspections in the Industrial Sector and 45 inspections related to Diesel Generator (DG) sets.

As part of the reporting period, a special inspection drive was conducted in Nuh, Haryana on 03.09.2026. Eight teams of the Commission's Flying Squads, along with District Administration and Police personnel and officers of the Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB), inspected a total of 35 premises. Of these, 13 were found compliant, while 7 units were found locked and are to be re-inspected by the concerned State Pollution Control Board. The recommended actions include personal hearing in 1 case, sealing of a DG set in 1 case, issuance of orders in 7 cases and imposition of Environmental Compensation (EC) in 6 cases.

Based on the violations reported by the concerned sectors, actions have been proposed in the reported cases. These include closure of 3 C&D projects and 1 industrial unit; sealing of 25 DG sets across C&D sites, industrial units and other units; and issuance of orders/directions for compliance in 1 C&D case, 2 industrial cases and 3 DG-related cases involving 10 DG sets. Environmental Compensation (EC) has also been proposed in 2 industrial cases. Other cases have been identified for appropriate action, including issuance of letters to project proponents, re-inspection and prosecution, and forwarding of cases to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), as applicable.

The status of resumption orders issued after the previous ETF meeting was also reviewed. As on 10.09.2026, a total of 6 resumption orders had been issued after the last ETF meeting, comprising 1 Industrial Unit and 5 C&D sites. State-wise, 3 resumption orders were issued in Haryana and 3 in Uttar Pradesh.

The updated cumulative enforcement status as on 14.09.2026 was also reviewed. The Flying Squads of the Commission have so far carried out inspections at 28,547 units/projects/entities across NCR. Based on these inspections, 1,829 Closure Directions have been issued, out of which 1,479 Resumption Orders have been issued after verification of compliance. Further, 126 cases have been transferred to the respective State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) for final decision, while 224 entities remain under examination for issuance of resumption orders.

The Commission reiterated the need for continued strengthening of enforcement, timely verification of compliance and close coordination among implementing agencies for effective implementation of the prescribed norms. It also emphasised expeditious enforcement action, strict compliance monitoring and continued inspections across priority sectors, including Industrial Units, C&D activities and DG sets, to ensure effective mitigation of air pollution across the NCR.

2310538.title: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Organises 12th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad
2310538.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Organises 12th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad
Six Districts Showcase Innovative Practices on Source Sustainability, Behaviour Change through IEC activities, Grievance Redressal Mechanism and Convergence
Posted On: 15 SEP 2026 5:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised the 12th edition of the District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad today through video conferencing, bringing together senior officials, District Collectors/ District Magistrates/ Deputy Commissioners, to deliberate on accelerating the implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and sharing of best practices.

The Samvad was chaired by Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS. Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM) and Senior Officers from SWSM and DDWS were also present during the Samvad.

Addressing the occasion, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, emphasized the importance of regular monthly District Water and Sanitation Mission (DWSM) meetings to review scheme progress, service delivery, water quality, and source sustainability under JJM 2.0. He stressed that completed schemes should be handed over to Gram Panchayats through the Jal Arpan programme after the prescribed trial run and proper documentation, thereby promoting community ownership and sustainable operation and maintenance. He urged districts to actively involve MPs, MLAs, and other public representatives through Jal Arpan ceremonies, DISHA meetings, and DWSM reviews to enhance transparency and public confidence in rural water supply systems. He also highlighted the need for timely utilization of JJM 2.0 funds, accurate reporting of physical and financial progress, and preparation of District and State Improvement Plans to address service gaps. Further, he encouraged the use of the Decision Support System (DSS) for planning source sustainability measures such as rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge, while underscoring that regular monitoring of scheme functionality, water quality, and sustainability interventions is essential to ensure reliable and sustainable drinking water services for all rural households.

The progress and best practices of six selected districts, Shahdol (Madhya Pradesh), Samba (Jammu & Kashmir), Hooghly (West Bengal), Dhamtari (Chhattisgarh), Fatehgarh Sahib (Punjab) and North & Middle Andaman (Andaman & Nicobar Islands) were also presented by the respective District Collectors/District Magistrates/District Commissioners to facilitate cross-learning and support other districts in strengthening implementation under JJM 2.0.
Innovative Best Practices shared by six districts through presentations by the respective District Collector/ District Magistrate/ Deputy Commissioner:

  • Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh- Sh. Parth Jaiswal, District Collector informed that civil and electrical works for the water supply schemes have largely been completed, and the remaining works are expected to be commissioned by November 2026. Emphasis was laid on conducting weekly reviews to ensure timely completion of all Single Village Schemes (SVSs) and Multi Village Schemes (MVSs). Out of 544 completed SVSs, 405 have already been handed over, while 35 more are planned for handover on 2 October 2026 through the Jal Arpan programme. The district has set a target to achieve full completion and functionality of all rural water supply schemes by December 2026 and to declare the district fully functional by 26 January 2027. The district also showcased best practices, including a digital platform for overhead tank cleaning and maintenance, an online mechanism for collection of water and sanitation charges through UPI and net banking, and systems to strengthen Gram Panchayat-led operation and maintenance. These initiatives are helping improve transparency, service delivery, revenue collection, and long-term sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure.

  • Samba, Jammu & Kashmir- Smt Ayushi Sudan, Deputy Commissioner presented Samba as a model district under Jal Jeevan Mission, despite facing significant water management challenges due to diverse geographical conditions and dependence on groundwater sources. Through JJM, the district increased Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) coverage with prescribed service levels from about 23% to nearly 70%, adding around 35,000 new tap connections. The district implemented 130 water supply schemes, supported by filtration plants, tube wells, dug wells, pumping stations, and storage infrastructure. Key challenges included difficult hilly terrain, declining groundwater levels, source sustainability concerns, power supply constraints, land-related issues, and the high operation and maintenance requirements of water supply systems. To address these challenges, the district adopted location-specific solutions based on local hydrogeological conditions. Several successful interventions were highlighted, including the revival of a 60-year-old dug well at the revered Uttar Behni Temple, which now provides drinking water to hundreds of households, and the development of customized schemes for remote hilly villages through a combination of filtration plants and tube wells to ensure universal coverage.

  • Hooghly, West Bengal- Sh. Khursheed Ali Qadri, District Magistrate showcased the district’s substantial progress in creating drinking water infrastructure, the district shifted its focus towards community participation, service assessment, and grievance redressal to ensure sustainable service delivery under Jal Jeevan Mission. Under the Jal Seva Abhiyan, village-level service assessments were conducted by Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), followed by validation exercises. The findings and suggested improvements were incorporated into the District Improvement Plan and submitted to the State Government. A strong emphasis was also placed on community awareness through Self-Help Groups (SHGs), with meetings, workshops, and campaigns involving nearly seven lakh women. These initiatives focused on water conservation, efficient water use, source sustainability, and reducing water wastage. To strengthen accountability, the district established a robust grievance redressal mechanism, receiving complaints through multiple channels, including helplines, emails, public representatives, and government platforms. Dedicated public hearing days are organized every week to address drinking water-related grievances promptly. Strict action has also been taken against illegal water connections and unauthorized usage to prevent water losses and ensure equitable distribution. Regular District Water and Sanitation Committee (DWSC) and DISHA meetings are being conducted with active participation of public representatives to review JJM implementation, address concerns, and undertake corrective measures. These efforts have significantly improved community engagement, transparency, service delivery, and public confidence in rural drinking water systems.

​​​​​​​

  • Dhamtari, Chhattisgarh- Sh. Abhinash Mishra, District Collector showcased that the district reported significant progress in the implementation of MVSs, with the majority of schemes already completed and the remaining works expected to be completed after obtaining necessary clearances, particularly in forest and tiger reserve areas. To ensure effective operation and maintenance (O&M), regular DWSM meetings are being conducted twice a month, focusing on scheme sustainability, convergence activities, payment issues, and service delivery improvements. The district has strengthened community ownership by ensuring active participation of VWSCs, with user charges being collected online based on population served. Gram Panchayats have been entrusted with the day-to-day O&M of water supply assets. Special emphasis has been placed on awareness generation through SHGs and community mobilization, with women playing a leading role in water governance. More than two-thirds of the Sarpanches and community representatives involved in these initiatives are women. A notable success story highlighted was a solar-powered Single Village Scheme in a remote tribal habitation, which has significantly improved access to drinking water in difficult terrain. The initiative received wide public appreciation and demonstrated how community participation, renewable energy, and decentralized management can contribute to sustainable rural drinking water service delivery.

​​​​​​​

  • Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab- Dr. Sona Thind, Deputy Commissioner highlighted the district’s successful achievement of 100%  FHTC coverage, ensuring tap water supply to all 78,475 rural households across 429 villages, along with full coverage of schools and Anganwadi centres. Building upon this achievement, the district has shifted its focus towards maintaining service quality, with nearly 80% of rural households receiving more than 70 lpcd of water, exceeding the JJM benchmark of 55 lpcd. To address groundwater depletion and water quality concerns, the district implemented a major 12 MLD surface water project drawing water from the Rajpura Distributary. The project serves 92 villages and has significantly benefited fluoride-affected areas by providing safe drinking water to over 86,000 people through an extensive pipeline network. The district has also adopted IoT-based real-time monitoring systems and a dedicated grievance redressal mechanism to ensure continuous service delivery and prompt response to complaints. Regular DWSM meetings, community participation through Gram Panchayats and VWSCs, and structured planning have strengthened local ownership of water supply systems. A strong emphasis has been placed on water quality surveillance, with NABL-accredited laboratories conducting regular testing and women-led community monitoring through Field Testing Kits (FTKs). Through a combination of surface water infrastructure, digital monitoring, community participation, and rigorous quality testing, the district has developed a sustainable model for maintaining safe and reliable drinking water services under Jal Jeevan Mission.

  • North and Middle Andaman, Andaman & Nicobar Islands- Sh. Sushant Padha, Deputy Commissioner highlighted the district's achievement of 100% FHTC coverage, covering all villages and approximately 24,400 households under Jal Jeevan Mission. A total of eight JJM schemes were completed with an expenditure of about ₹5.2 crore, ensuring universal rural water supply coverage. Given the district's unique island geography and recurring summer water scarcity, monthly DWSM meetings are being conducted to review water availability and plan long-term sustainability measures. Discussions focus on rejuvenation of existing water sources, construction of ponds, ring wells, and water treatment plants, as well as expediting Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) clearances, which often delay project implementation due to the district's extensive forest cover. To address seasonal water shortages, the district has adopted a decentralized approach by creating village-level water storage structures and enhancing local water security through convergence with MGNREGA and other development programmes. The administration is also working closely with ISRO's National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) to identify and study spring sources, assess groundwater feasibility, and improve recharge measures. The district has placed strong emphasis on water quality monitoring, with regular sample testing through WQMIS-enabled laboratories and continuous surveillance of drinking water sources. A proactive grievance redressal mechanism, supported by digital communication platforms and local stakeholder networks, helps ensure prompt resolution of complaints, including a focus on zero-leakage service delivery. Awareness campaigns on water conservation, social water audits, community training, and public outreach through print and social media are being conducted extensively to promote responsible water use and strengthen long-term source sustainability in the island district.

In his concluding remarks, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM appreciated the presentations made by Districts and urged that all Mission Directors to actively participate in the upcoming Skilling and Nal Jal Mitra Programme discussions by coordinating with the State Skill Development Departments and sharing inputs before the virtual meeting scheduled on 21 September 2026. Further, he stated that States/UTs were also advised to commence geo-tagging of rural water supply sources from 2 October 2026. Further, Jal Arpan activities should be organized on 2 October 2026 across the maximum possible number of Gram Panchayats, with details of participating GPs to be shared with the Department by 20 September 2026. States/UTs were also directed to initiate post-monsoon testing of water supply sources from 2 October 2026. The meeting concluded with appreciation for the efforts of all participating States and Districts towards effective implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
